question: Where does catastrophic forgetting appear behaviorally and internally across sequentially fine-tuned 2026 language models, and can updates restricted to the orthogonal complement of historical activation subspaces preserve old tasks without sacrificing new-task adaptation?

key_findings.claim: Author study design: the paper reports a 20-model coding-to-math-to-medical sequence, using output drift for ten closed models and CKA, routing drift, weight drift, attention entropy, and activation patching for ten open-weight models.
key_findings.evidence: The cohorts span reported 27B-to-1.6T open models and ten proprietary APIs. The sequence uses AdamW, learning rate 2×10^-5, cosine decay, and batch size 128. RADL flags layers whose CKA is below or routing JSD above thresholds, then LRCP is applied to selected circuits. However, no task dataset sizes/splits, epochs, sequence lengths, threshold values, activation sampling protocol, checkpoint IDs, hardware, seeds for open models, or model-specific adaptation procedure is supplied, so this is a description rather than an executable protocol.

anchors.section: Sections 4.1-4.3, model lists and task sequence

key_findings.claim: Author-reported closed-model result: every proprietary model loses substantial Task A coding accuracy after the math and medical updates, with reported net losses from 27.7 to 45.9 points.
key_findings.evidence: Table 1 reports GPT-5.5 High changing from 94.1 to 65.4 (-28.7) with SOD 0.254, Claude Fable 5 from 92.4 to 61.2 (-31.2) with SOD 0.289, and GPT-4.5 from 81.3 to 35.4 (-45.9) with SOD 0.498. These exact values have no reported variance, task sample count, API endpoint/snapshot identifier, or disclosed route by which each closed model was sequentially parameter-adapted, so they must be treated strictly as unverified author-reported measurements.

anchors.section: Table 1, ten closed-model accuracy and SOD rows
Section 8.3, frozen snapshot and N=5 claims

key_findings.claim: Author-reported open-model result: the claimed coding losses are 34.3-47.2 points, mid-layer CKA is 0.412-0.612, and down-projection matrices have the largest normalized Frobenius drift in every table row.
key_findings.evidence: Table 2 ranges from DeepSeek-V4-Pro at 88.5 to 54.2 (-34.3), CKA 0.612, RGD 0.314, to Qwen 3.6-27B at 78.4 to 31.2 (-47.2), CKA 0.412. Table 3 reports W_down drift of 6.89-12.89×10^-3, above W_gate/up 5.12-10.23, W_query 2.54-4.56, and W_value 1.21-2.45 for every model. The paper interprets this association as localized mid-layer/MLP susceptibility, but no uncertainty, normalization formula for D_F, or cross-layer activation sample construction is given.

anchors.section: Figures 1-3, attention, trajectory, and activation-patching plots

key_findings.claim: Reviewer causal audit: the paper's activation-patching and entropy figures do not quantitatively establish the claimed three mechanisms of forgetting.
key_findings.evidence: Figure 3 says saved baseline activations are patched into the A-to-B model on 500 SWE-bench samples, but it supplies only a plotted recovery curve with generic layer-group indices, no exact values, intervention controls, patching granularity, variance, or model identity. Figures 1, 2, 4, 5, and 8 similarly show unlabeled aggregate trajectories or trends. Correlated CKA, routing JSD, weight movement, attention entropy, and source accuracy can all be consequences of task adaptation; without controlled ablations they do not distinguish gradient interference, representation collapse, and loss-landscape flattening as independent causes.

key_findings.claim: Author-reported LRCP result: on Llama 4 Scout after coding-to-math adaptation, targeted activation-subspace projection gives the best reported retention/plasticity trade-off among five methods.
key_findings.evidence: LRCP forms P=I-U_k U_k^T from an SVD of historical activations and right-multiplies selected-layer gradients by P. Table 4 reports Task A/Task B accuracy of 74.8/75.1 at 1.09× overhead and 1.62% active parameters, versus replay 72.1/74.3 at 1.28×, LoRA 58.4/70.1, EWC 56.1/71.2, and full fine-tuning 35.1/76.8. No seeds, confidence intervals, equal-compute details, calibration-set size, or RADL selection thresholds accompany these exact values.

key_findings.claim: Author negative result: LRCP exhibits a clear stability-plasticity trade-off as projection rank grows.
key_findings.evidence: Table 5 moves from rank ratio 0.05 at Task A/B 48.4/76.4, drift 8.12×10^-3, and 3.1 convergence epochs to 0.20 at 74.8/75.1, 1.62, and 3.7, then 0.40 at 78.1/61.4, 0.39, and 5.8. Thus stronger protection continuously improves retention and lowers drift but, above 0.20, sharply damages math adaptation and slows convergence; 0.20 is a selected operating point rather than a dominance result.

key_findings.claim: Internal metric contradiction: SOD is introduced as a distance between token probability distributions but operationally described as a sentence embedding of top-k sampled tokens.
key_findings.evidence: Equation 3 applies Phi to P_theta(y|x), suggesting an embedding of an entire probability distribution. The immediately following definition says Phi is a sentence-level embedding vector of top-k sampled tokens, but it never names the embedding model, top-k value, sampling-to-sentence construction, probability weighting, or aggregation across N=5. A sample-string embedding and a distributional distance are not interchangeable, so the reported SOD values cannot be reconstructed or interpreted as representation drift from the given equation.

key_findings.claim: Reproducibility contradiction: the paper reports parameter fine-tuning and internal-style probability metrics for closed APIs without specifying any reproducible adaptation or observation interface.
key_findings.evidence: All 20 models are said to follow the same AdamW sequential fine-tuning pipeline, while the closed cohort is only described as API-accessible and later as frozen June 2026 snapshots 'where accessible.' There are no endpoint IDs, fine-tuning job IDs, snapshot timestamps, provider-specific procedures, top-logprob settings, dataset uploads, or explanation of how the stated optimizer/batch size applies to proprietary systems. The five repeated samples address output nondeterminism but not whether the same model state or parameter update was measured.

anchors.section: Sections 4.2-4.3, closed cohort and common fine-tuning protocol
Section 5.1 and Table 1, sequentially adapted API claims

key_findings.claim: Related-work and complexity contradiction: LRCP's claimed distinction from GPM misstates the direct predecessor, and a one-time SVD does not make every training-step projection O(1).
key_findings.evidence: Section 2.2 says GPM/OGP suffer continuous online SVD recalculation at every training step, but the official GPM record describes a single-shot SVD after each task and stored activation bases. LRCP's new restriction to RADL-selected circuits can reduce cost, yet applying a d-by-k projector or its factored equivalent still scales with activation width, rank, batch/tokens, and selected layers. Equation 5 therefore supports eliminating repeated decomposition, not the literal O(1) backpropagation-complexity claim.

key_findings.claim: Internal numerical-language contradiction: the abstract says LRCP 'mitigates up to 94.2% of ancestral capabilities,' which reverses the intended semantics and is not reproduced by the visible table.
key_findings.evidence: Mitigating a capability means reducing it; the intended claim appears to be retaining capability. For Llama 4 Scout, Table 2 gives initial Task A 79.5 and Table 4 gives LRCP Task A 74.8, which is 94.09% retention, conventionally 94.1%, not 94.2%. No other LRCP per-model retention table supports the stated 'up to' value, so neither the wording nor exact percentage is traceable from the reported results.

key_findings.claim: Artifact audit: the declared public code/supplement is not actually locatable from the paper, and several central citations cannot be source-checked from the bibliography as written.
key_findings.evidence: Data availability says the codebase, activation pipelines, and analysis scripts are publicly accessible, while Appendix A only says materials are at 'the project's repository'; neither section supplies a URL, DOI, archive identifier, commit, or artifact version. The appendix contains no supplementary results. References used to motivate drift/localization include records with no DOI/arXiv/URL and atypical or malformed metadata, while GPM/OGD are discussed without their actual papers being cited. These omissions block independent verification of data, models, plots, and the closest algorithmic antecedents.

method.core_idea: Measure behavioral and internal drift after a fixed coding-to-math-to-medical sequence, identify high-drift transformer circuits with CKA and routing divergence, then preserve historical activation directions only in those circuits by projecting new gradients into an orthogonal complement.
method.mechanism: For open models, RADL compares baseline and adapted activations layer by layer, flagging low-CKA or high-RGD blocks. Historical activations for flagged circuits are decomposed once as U_k; LRCP applies P=I-U_kU_k^T to their gradients during the next task. Closed models are assessed through SOD over purported output distributions/semantic embeddings. The paper compares source retention, target accuracy, reported overhead, and a rank-ratio sweep on Llama 4 Scout.
assumptions: All named checkpoints and proprietary snapshots are exactly identifiable and accessible, despite the absence of model IDs, release records, or access details.
Closed-source systems can be sequentially adapted under a protocol meaningfully comparable to full-parameter AdamW fine-tuning of open models.
Sentence embeddings of top-k sampled tokens form a stable proxy for output-distribution and representation drift across different APIs.
The unspecified activation samples, layer normalization, HSIC estimator, and CKA aggregation yield comparable scores across architectures and scales.
Jensen-Shannon routing drift measures harmful expert reassignment rather than useful adaptation or changes in token distribution.
RADL thresholds identify causal forgetting circuits rather than merely high-change layers, and the same calibration data are not leaking evaluation-specific information.
Historical activation principal directions are the directions that should be protected, and their orthogonal complement retains enough plasticity for the new task.
One coding-to-math-to-medical order, unreported seeds, and one Llama 4 Scout mitigation table generalize across the claimed 20-model landscape.

techniques.role: Compares layer activation geometry before and after sequential adaptation in open models.
Measures changes in MoE expert-assignment probabilities.
Attempts a black-box proxy for proprietary-model drift using sampled outputs and sentence embeddings.
Restores saved baseline activations to test whether selected layer groups recover coding performance.
Flags layers crossing CKA or routing-drift thresholds as susceptible circuits.
Constructs a low-rank basis U_k from prior-task calibration activations.
Projects gradients at selected circuits into I-U_kU_k^T to reduce interference.
Varies protected-subspace rank to expose retention, adaptation, drift, and convergence trade-offs.

evaluations.setting: Ten closed-source models after a reported coding-to-math-to-medical adaptation sequence.
evaluations.metric: Initial and post-sequence Task A accuracy, absolute loss, and mean SOD.
evaluations.result: Reported loss ranges from -27.7 points for Meta Muse Spark (90.1 to 62.4, SOD 0.241) to -45.9 for GPT-4.5 (81.3 to 35.4, SOD 0.498); no uncertainty or reproducible adaptation identifiers are provided.
evaluations.baseline: Each model's initial Task A state; there is no no-update temporal API control or common accessible checkpoint.

evaluations.setting: Ten open-weight models after the same reported three-task sequence.
evaluations.metric: Task A loss, mid-layer CKA, and MoE routing JSD.
evaluations.result: Task A losses are 34.3-47.2 points, CKA 0.412-0.612, and RGD 0.314-0.512 where applicable. Exact rows are supplied but not seeds, intervals, activation sample counts, or checkpoint hashes.
evaluations.baseline: Each model's Task A checkpoint before Task B/C adaptation.

evaluations.setting: Projection-matrix drift across all ten open models.
evaluations.metric: Mean normalized Frobenius drift D_F×10^-3 for W_query, W_value, W_gate/up, and W_down.
evaluations.result: W_down is largest in all ten rows (6.89-12.89), followed by W_gate/up (5.12-10.23), while W_value is smallest (1.21-2.45). The normalization formula and uncertainty are absent.
evaluations.baseline: Within-model comparison among four projection types.

evaluations.setting: Activation patching on a 500-sample SWE-bench subset plus attention/weight/routing visual diagnostics.
evaluations.metric: Task A recovery rate, attention KL/entropy, CKA-derived susceptibility, and t-SNE trajectories.
evaluations.result: The figures visually claim peak recovery/susceptibility in selected middle groups and higher early attention entropy, but provide no tabulated values, model/control details, or uncertainty sufficient to quantify the causal effect.
evaluations.baseline: Adapted activations versus saved Task A activations; generic layer groups 1-10.

evaluations.metric: Final Task A/Task B accuracy, training overhead, and active-parameter percentage.
evaluations.baseline: Standard full fine-tuning, rank-16 LoRA, EWC, and 10% replay.

evaluations.setting: LRCP protected-rank sweep on Llama 4 Scout.
evaluations.metric: Task A/Task B accuracy, D_F×10^-3, and convergence epochs.
evaluations.result: Rank 0.05 gives 48.4/76.4/8.12/3.1; 0.20 gives 74.8/75.1/1.62/3.7; 0.40 gives 78.1/61.4/0.39/5.8, showing that retention and lower drift come at a steep plasticity/convergence cost above 0.20.

evaluations.metric: N=5 repeated outputs at temperature zero on frozen June 2026 snapshots where accessible.
evaluations.result: The paper says it averages five semantic embedding vectors, but gives no variance, endpoint/snapshot identifiers, exact dates, per-provider top-logprob support, or frozen-control measurements.
evaluations.baseline: No explicit version-drift or repeated unadapted API baseline.

limitations: Author-acknowledged: closed APIs remain nondeterministic and subject to version drift even at temperature zero.
Author-acknowledged: proprietary internal parameters are unavailable, so the closed cohort can only be analyzed behaviorally.
Reviewer-identified: no exact open checkpoint revisions/hashes or proprietary endpoint/snapshot/job IDs are reported for any of the 20 systems.
Reviewer-identified: the paper never explains how closed APIs are sequentially fine-tuned, how a common AdamW/batch protocol applies to them, or how full token distributions are obtained.
Reviewer-identified: task datasets are named only by broad benchmark families; sizes, splits, prompts, epochs, sequence lengths, licenses, preprocessing, and contamination controls are missing.
Reviewer-identified: CKA's HSIC estimator, layer/token aggregation, normalization, calibration sample size, and RADL thresholds are unspecified.
Reviewer-identified: SOD conflates output distributions with sentence embeddings of sampled tokens and omits its embedding model and k.
Reviewer-identified: tables and figures provide no open-model seeds, error bars, hypothesis tests, or raw measurements; N=5 is mentioned only for closed output sampling.
Reviewer-identified: activation patching is insufficiently described and reported only as an unlabeled plot, so the claimed causal mechanisms remain unquantified.
Reviewer-identified: the same drift analysis appears to select LRCP circuits and justify/evaluate the method, with no held-out localization set or post-selection correction.
Reviewer-identified: mitigation is evaluated numerically on one model and only the A-to-B segment, not the full A-to-B-to-C sequence or all claimed architectures.
Reviewer-identified: the one-time SVD may reduce decomposition cost, but storage and every-step projection still scale with selected layers, width, rank, tokens, and batch size.
Reviewer-identified: claimed public code and supplement have no URL or version, and proprietary logs are available only on request.
Reviewer-identified: the reference list omits the actual GPM/OGD records while mischaracterizing GPM and includes multiple identifier-free or malformed records central to the narrative.
Reviewer-identified: the 94.2% abstract statement has reversed wording and no exact derivation from the visible results.
failure_modes: Protecting too small a subspace leaves high drift and poor source retention; protecting too much collapses target accuracy and slows convergence.
RADL can label useful adaptation as harmful drift, causing LRCP to freeze the circuits most needed for transfer.
A calibration set that is small, task-specific, or reused in evaluation can produce a brittle or post-hoc protected basis.
Activation directions can rotate across tasks, making a static U_k obsolete in a longer stream.
Projecting only flagged layers can move interference into unprotected layers or MoE routers.
Closed API version changes or sampling variance can be mistaken for catastrophic forgetting when no time-matched unadapted control exists.
Embedding sampled top-k strings can register style/length drift rather than capability or probability-distribution drift.
Cross-model CKA/RGD values can be incomparable when tokenization, width, routing topology, layers, and activation normalization differ.
Uncontrolled task difficulty and training budgets can create the reported model ranking without reflecting architectural resilience.
A purportedly low-overhead projector can become memory- or compute-dominant at hundreds of billions of parameters when rank and selected-layer counts scale.
reusable_insights: Localization should precede protection: applying anti-forgetting constraints only where interventions show causal recovery can improve the stability-plasticity budget.
Always pair a drift statistic with task performance and intervention evidence; representation change alone is not forgetting.
A factored projector I-UU^T avoids materializing a dense d-by-d matrix, but its per-step cost should be reported in rank-aware FLOPs and memory.
Rank sweeps are more informative than a single optimum because they expose whether an anti-forgetting method merely trades plasticity for retention.
For black-box models, archive exact endpoint IDs, timestamps, request/response logs, logprob settings, and unadapted temporal controls before interpreting output changes causally.
Define whether a metric compares distributions, logits, samples, or embeddings; do not slide between these objects in one equation.
Closest-predecessor audits matter: a localized version of activation-subspace projection should be compared directly against one-shot GPM/OGD and prior LLM SVD preservation under equal compute.
open_questions: Can the reported model checkpoints, task data, fine-tuning jobs, cached activations, and API logs be independently reproduced from a versioned public artifact?
What exact adaptation interfaces and optimizer controls were used for each proprietary model?
Does LRCP outperform one-shot GPM, OGD, and Principal Subspace Preserving when all methods protect the same layers and use equal rank/memory?
Are RADL-selected layers stable across random seeds, task orders, calibration sets, and architectures?
Does activation patching at those layers recover old-task accuracy without directly reintroducing old-task answers or harming the new task?
How does LRCP perform through Task C and over ten or more tasks when protected subspaces accumulate?
Can a preregistered, held-out localization protocol avoid using the same drift evidence to choose and validate the protected circuits?
What is SOD after specifying a concrete embedding model and k, and how does it correlate with proper logit KL, calibrated accuracy, and human judgments?
What computation and memory do U_k storage and factored gradient projection require as functions of width, rank, tokens, and selected layers?
Which cited records and public repository were intended by the identifier-free bibliography and data-availability statements?

competitive_landscape.title: Gradient Projection Memory for Continual Learning
competitive_landscape.difference: GPM already performs a single-shot SVD of prior-task neural activations, stores subspace bases, and projects later gradients orthogonally to those important directions. LRCP's narrow possible advance is RADL-based restriction to selected LLM circuits; the target paper's claim that GPM continuously recomputes SVD every training step is contradicted by GPM's official record.

competitive_landscape.title: Orthogonal Gradient Descent for Continual Learning
competitive_landscape.difference: OGD already restricts new-task updates to a subspace where outputs on previous tasks do not change, using stored gradient directions rather than historical activation SVD. LRCP changes the protected object and localizes application to selected transformer circuits, but not the core orthogonal-complement update principle.

competitive_landscape.title: Preserving Principal Subspaces to Reduce Catastrophic Forgetting in Fine-tuning
competitive_landscape.difference: Franke et al. already use SVD to protect principal weight-matrix subspaces during LLM fine-tuning without old training data, directly anticipating low-rank orthogonal preservation in this domain. LRCP instead builds bases from historical activations and selects circuits via drift diagnostics; a fair novelty test would compare these choices head-to-head, which the target paper does not do or cite.
competitive_landscape.source_version: OpenReview forum XoWtroECJU, ICLR 2024 ME-FoMo workshop poster revision (modified 2024-05-05)

competitive_landscape.title: LoRA Learns Less and Forgets Less
competitive_landscape.difference: Biderman et al. quantify that low-rank LLM adaptation preserves out-of-domain capabilities better but learns less than full fine-tuning across instruction tuning and 20B-token continued pretraining, including the rank gap of learned updates. LRCP reports a better single-table trade-off than rank-16 LoRA, but does not match that study's scale, domains, budgets, or uncertainty and supplies no rank-matched LoRA sweep.

competitive_landscape.title: Revisiting Catastrophic Forgetting in Large Language Model Tuning
competitive_landscape.difference: Li et al. directly connect LLM forgetting to loss-landscape flatness and mitigate it with sharpness-aware minimization on three fine-tuning datasets and multiple scales. The target paper claims attention/MLP/routing mechanisms and localized projection instead, but does not compare against SAM or provide sufficient controlled evidence to distinguish its mechanism from this prior one.

competitive_landscape.title: Lottery Ticket Adaptation: Mitigating Destructive Interference in LLMs
competitive_landscape.difference: LoTA identifies and updates a sparse LLM subnetwork to reduce destructive interference across instruction, reasoning, math, and summarization tasks and supports task-vector merging. LRCP likewise activates only 1.62% of parameters but chooses them through drift localization and constrains directions rather than optimizing a sparse ticket; the target omits the closest sparse-update baseline.

competitive_landscape.title: Retaining by Doing: The Role of On-Policy Data in Mitigating Forgetting
competitive_landscape.difference: Chen et al. compare SFT and RL across Llama/Qwen tasks and causally isolate on-policy data as the main driver of reduced forgetting, including approximately on-policy alternatives. The target evaluates only supervised-style parameter interventions; without on-policy training baselines it cannot show LRCP is preferable to a change in learning paradigm.

competitive_landscape.title: Overcoming Catastrophic Forgetting in Neural Networks
competitive_landscape.difference: EWC protects parameters in proportion to estimated old-task importance and is the principal regularization baseline in Table 4. LRCP protects low-rank activation directions only in selected circuits and reports lower overhead/better retention, but the absence of tuning ranges, uncertainty, and equal-compute details prevents the single result from establishing superiority.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The paper claims the first systematic mid-2026 comparison of catastrophic forgetting across ten closed and ten open frontier models, localizes attention/MLP/MoE drift mechanistically, and introduces LRCP as a low-overhead targeted subspace intervention retaining up to 94.2% of ancestral capability.
novelty_assessment.evidence: It presents five numeric tables, eight diagnostic/trade-off figures, CKA/RGD/SOD definitions, a RADL procedure, activation patching, and LRCP equations. The strongest visible mitigation evidence is one Llama 4 Scout table at 74.8 coding and 75.1 math with reported 1.09× overhead and a five-point rank sweep.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The plausible algorithmic novelty is only the combination of drift-based layer selection with prior activation-subspace orthogonal gradient projection in an LLM/MoE framing. GPM already supplies one-shot activation SVD and gradient projection, OGD supplies the orthogonal update principle, and Principal Subspace Preserving already applies SVD-based protection to LLM fine-tuning. The broad empirical and mechanistic novelty is not established because model/data/adaptation identities, metrics, uncertainty, code, and intervention details are insufficient for reproduction; the closed-API protocol and SOD definition are internally incomplete, GPM is mischaracterized, and the 94.2% claim is neither worded nor derived correctly.

reviewer_notes: Primary full-text review covered every one of the 13 PDF pages in the pinned arXiv:2601.18699v2 artifact: cover/highlights, all main sections, Equations 1-5, Algorithm 1, all five tables and eight figures, discussion/limitations, declarations/data availability, the nominal Appendix A, and the full references. Appendix A contains only a one-sentence pointer to an unnamed project repository; there are no supplemental proofs, tables, maps, code locators, or additional experiments in the artifact. The fulltext index pin was checked verbatim: PDF SHA-256 88370bc59ab4db15c0f80f6ba5f40664cd9f1c5a0487c886123a949b4d942c64, text SHA-256 e7682617116e26911c754345071710b7e9f9e4e2bd578513a97a78d9d51e461c, 13/13 pages with usable text and no missing pages; a fresh official arXiv v2 PDF independently reproduced the indexed PDF hash on 2026-08-23. Confidence 0.88 reflects high confidence in what the artifact says and in the internal audit, not confidence that its empirical numbers are reproducible: exact checkpoint/API identities, adaptation jobs, datasets, metric implementations, uncertainty, and public artifacts are missing. Author-stated API nondeterminism/version drift is separated from reviewer-identified protocol and validity limits. Negative evidence (rank-protection plasticity collapse and router-freezing claim) and contradictions (SOD object mismatch, closed-API fine-tuning gap, GPM history, O(1), 94.2%, and missing repository) are retained. Eight exact-version direct primary competitors were checked on 2026-08-23 through official arXiv or OpenReview records.
